what_happened: On a docs job (probably a glossary), the user corrected Athena's first reading. The user supplied a list of terms Athena had misread, each with the source that defines it. Examples: "planning" meant planning each job's design before coding, but Athena built queue ordering. "job" means one request to one landing, not a whole engagement. "Athena" can mean the whole system or the strategy and learning role inside Olympus. "Hermes" can mean the orchestration role or Hermes Agent. "landed" means merged on main through a verified pull request. The user also corrected how to refer to Sri: by name or as "they", never "he" or "she". An earlier reading, for job 20261017-173504-91ys, had called Sri "he".
cause: Athena reads the project's overloaded terms by their common meaning, not by what the owner's own documents (BRIEF.md addenda, the Olympus note, the study) say they mean. Nothing in the system keeps a list of project terms with their meanings and sources, so each reading starts without one. Nothing records the owner's pronoun preference either. The same misread therefore came back in a second job, which shows that a correction to one reading does not carry over to the next.
prevention: Keep a glossary of project terms and owner conventions in the repo. It would hold the terms above, each with its meaning and source, plus the rule to refer to Sri by name or as "they". Load it into every reading step. Add a check that flags any reading using a glossary term in a sense other than the glossary's, or using gendered pronouns for Sri. When the user corrects a term, add it to the glossary as part of closing the correction.
proposed_request: Create a project glossary file in the repo that records each ambiguous term with its meaning and the source that defines it. Seed it with: planning (planning each job's design before coding, BRIEF.md addendum 2026-10-16 "Speed, planning first"; Athena built queue ordering, D105); job (one request to one landing, not a whole engagement or product, addendum 2026-10-17: Olympus); Athena (the whole system versus the strategy and learning role inside Olympus, same addendum); Hermes (the orchestration role versus Hermes Agent, the second studied system, Part 2 S1); product versus system (the study's files, site generator and Pages workflow versus everything else, the Olympus relay note); landed (merged on main through a verified pull request); Sri (the owner: refer to Sri by name or as they, never he or she). Make the reading step load the glossary. Add a code check that fails a reading which uses "he" or "she" for Sri. Done when the glossary is merged on main through a verified pull request, and a test reading that calls Sri "he" is rejected.
